> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 7b67774f7d9dee4d41659762c3d4cb4244448fcc && git checkout 7b67774f7d9dee4d41659762c3d4cb4244448fcc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759 c71a087e64086358935cae6c6d4f9f004ee85c6b && git checkout -B drift-repro 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759 && git merge --no-ff c71a087e64086358935cae6c6d4f9f004ee85c6b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Scope: packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/hono-body-refusal.test.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/hono-catch-all-raw-request.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/request-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/request-body-refusal.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/approvals.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/auth.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-outbox-plugin.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/src/hono-webhooks-redeliver.conformance.test.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/src/hono-approvals-act.conformance.test.ts, packages/adapters/hono/package.json, packages/adapters/hono/vitest.config.ts, tsup.config.ts, .changeset/config.json, .changeset/23914-hono-body-refusal.md, content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, and hono 4.13.12 (the lockfile's resolution for this package) dist/utils/body.js and dist/request.js. The changeset `.changeset/24042-hono-undeclared-body-refusal.md` is the prose face, judged in ②.

Net diff against the merge base `b1d5569d9`: 4 files, 396 insertions, 122 deletions; 1 added, 3 modified. The tree of `c71a087e6` is the tree of `f0c5d3bdc` (`47da01c42…`), so the two intermediate commits are history only; `.changeset/23914-hono-body-refusal.md` is byte-identical to the merge base (an empty diff). No `packages/spec` path, no governed path (the seven register rows in `check-governed-merges.mjs:1177-1183`, none hit), head repo is the base repo, 518 changed lines. Every hold-off of the claim `6225935648` holds: nothing under `plugin-hono-server`, `cloud-connection`, `plugin-auth`, `packages/spec`, `http-dispatcher.ts` or `runtime/src/domains` is in the file list.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. `readDispatchBody` is `readRequestBody`, branch for branch (`hono/src/index.ts:374-406` against `plugin-hono-server/src/request-body.ts:133-167`).** Right.

- Declared JSON (`includes('application/json')` on the lowered header, so a charset suffix and another case spelling match): text, blank is `{}`, unparseable is refused with `MALFORMED_JSON_BODY_MESSAGE`, unreadable with `UNREADABLE_BODY_MESSAGE`. Unchanged from #24005 except that the three statements now sit inside the JSON branch; the clone-or-cache choice (`raw.bodyUsed ? c.req.text() : raw.clone().text()`) is the one #24005 landed.
- A form (`mediaType` is the lowered header before the first `;`, trimmed; `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`): `parseBody(raw.clone())`, or `c.req.parseBody()` when something upstream already consumed the body. These are one function: in hono 4.13.12 `HonoRequest.parseBody(options)` is `parseBody(this, options)` (`dist/request.js:78-80`), and `parseBody` takes a raw `Request` as well as a `HonoRequest`, reads `Content-Type` off whichever headers it has, lowercases and splits on `;` exactly as the adapter does, and `parseFormData` reads `arrayBuffer()` on either (`dist/utils/body.js`). Default options on both doors (`all: false`), so a repeated name is its last value, as the raw-request form row pins. A throw out of `formData()` (a multipart body whose boundary does not match, or no boundary at all) is refused with `malformedFormMessage(mediaType)` on both doors; a malformed urlencoded body does not throw on either, so both answer 200 with the same fields (parity row, labelled as such).
- Any other media type, or none: nothing is read; `declaresBody(c)` decides between the refusal (`unreadMediaTypeMessage`) and `{}`. The forwarded request is untouched on this path.

**2. The mirrored prose is the twin's, word for word (`index.ts:463-500` against `request-body.ts:100-131`).** Compared: `NOT_EMPTY`, `MALFORMED_JSON_BODY_MESSAGE`, `UNREADABLE_BODY_MESSAGE`, `namedMediaType` (the same 64-plus-64 token-pair regex, `with no Content-Type` for the empty string, `with an unrecognised Content-Type` otherwise, so the only client-controlled fragment in any message stays a token pair), `malformedFormMessage`, `unreadMediaTypeMessage`, and `declaresBody` (`Content-Length` present and not blank: `Number(length) !== 0`; else `Transfer-Encoding` present). Identical. Right.

**3. Every refusal rides the refuse-on-read value and nothing else moved (`index.ts:408-441`, `:999-1016`, `:1055-1073`, `:723`).** Right. `DispatchBody`, `readable`, the `refusedOnRead` Proxy (every trap sets `read` and throws) and both arms are outside the diff: the catch-all reads for POST, PUT and PATCH only and dispatches GET, HEAD and DELETE with `undefined`; the `/auth/*` fallback reads for every method but GET and HEAD and hands those `{}`; after `dispatch()` or `handleAuth()` returns, `refusalRead()` wins over the domain's answer, and in the catch arm `read?.refusalRead() ?? err`; `thrownJson` renders through `declaredEnvelopeForThrow`, so the envelope is the declared two-key ADR-0112 one with the ledger code `INVALID_REQUEST`. So the three new refusals are answered only when a dispatched domain reads the body, after `dispatch()`'s gates: `body` is held in two handler-argument literals only (`http-dispatcher.ts:2890`, `:2989`), and `resolveRequestScope`, the ADR-0069 gate and membership run first (`:2905-2925`). Measured by the dev on the real plugin-webhooks member, hosted against the self-hosted mount over a socket: anonymous `text/plain`, `octet-stream` and no-`Content-Type` bodies answer `401` at both doors, signed-in garbage the member's own `400`, equal bytes on six rows. Consistent with the code read.

**4. The accept-set changes the diff implies, each named.**

- A body that declares neither JSON nor a form, when the request declares a body by its framing headers: FROM parsed as JSON when it parsed (#23914's step 4 honoured) and `{}` otherwise, TO refused when read, `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. The card's two rows (`:106`, `:109` of the base raw-request table) and step 4 (`:101`). Right, and the card's Done-when.
- A `+json` suffix type (`application/merge-patch+json`) is inside that row: it was parsed as JSON at base and is refused now, as on the twin. Right; the changeset names it.
- A form: FROM `{}` (the base raw-request row `:108`), TO its parsed fields; a form that does not parse, TO the refusal. Right: it is the twin's rule, which the card's Done-when names ("the way `plugin-hono-server` does") and the claim's file surface spells out ("`multipart/form-data` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` parsed from a clone"). What a domain then does with the fields is the domain's: measured on the data domain, a form query is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` where it read every row, a form create writes the form's fields where it wrote an empty row, a form PATCH applies where it changed nothing. No silent widening in any cell.
- No body declared, any media type: `{}`. Unchanged, except the one corner in ②.
- Declared JSON: unchanged (#24005). GET, HEAD and DELETE on the catch-all, GET and HEAD on `/auth/*`: unchanged.

**5. A forwarding domain still reads its own bytes.** Right. Both reading branches read a clone, the third reads nothing, so `c.req.raw` reaches `dispatch()` unread in every case: pinned per moved row with `bodyUsed === false` and the exact bytes, and the cache path (an upstream `c.req.parseBody()`) pinned separately. `/approvals/act` reads `context.request` only and answers a consumed body as a logged `500` (`approvals.ts:137-144`); the inbound hooks the same (`automation-hooks.ts:151-158`); `/webhooks/redeliver` checks the session and then `request.json()` through its facade (`webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:97-99`, `:548-558`); the legacy auth domain's `_body` is unread by design (`auth.ts:81-88`), so no answer changes on the `/auth/*` arm today. The two conformance pins that drive these doors through the real `createHonoApp` are outside the diff and still describe this head: `hono-webhooks-redeliver.conformance.test.ts` sends every row as `application/json` (`redeliver`, `:198-205`), so its `not JSON` row (`:240`) is a declared-JSON case this PR leaves as #24005 left it; `hono-approvals-act.conformance.test.ts:152` posts a real `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` form, now parsed from a clone while the member reads the unread original. The dev ran both files green (17 cases); CI's `Test Core (3/6)` is the gate (③).

**6. Published surface.** Nothing changes. `index.ts` exports the same seven statements (`:29`, `:35`, `:42`, `:51`, `:68`, `:278`, `:559`); `RequestBodyRefusal`, `DispatchBody`, `readable`, `refusedOnRead`, the messages and `declaresBody` are module-private; `package.json` is untouched (`exports` carries `"."` only). The new import `hono/utils/body` is hono's `./utils/*` export, present on every 4.x the peer range `^4.12.8` admits, and tsup's default leaves `dependencies` and `peerDependencies` external (root `tsup.config.ts`, no `noExternal`), which is the `require("hono/utils/body")` the dev read in the built CJS; `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint and Repo Gates` (`check:dts-closure`, `check:published-files`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` inside it) are green on the head. Right.

**7. Pins: every removed assertion is re-pinned with its new answer, and no pin loosens.** Right.

- `hono-body-refusal.test.ts`: the parity case is one 21-row table driven through BOTH doors (the hosted catch-all in front of a reader that answers a throw out of its read with its own `500`; a real `HonoHttpServer` route, resolved to source by the vitest alias, answering `req.body`), with `toEqual` on the whole body and `toBe` on the status: six declared-JSON rows, four form rows, eight other-media-type rows (step 4 twice, plain text, no `Content-Type` built from bytes so undici stamps nothing, `octet-stream`, `+json`, a non-token-pair type, `Transfer-Encoding` framing), three no-body rows. The four new reader rows, the `/auth/*` row and the malformed-multipart row each assert the refusal though the domain answered its own `500` and that nothing was read; the new forwarder row asserts the forwarder's own bytes and answer for a `text/plain` garbage body; the CONTROL form row expects the parsed fields. `expectRefused` still asserts the message never contains the body.
- `hono-catch-all-raw-request.test.ts`: the four rows that left the reference table (`:101`, `:106`, `:108`, `:109`) are each re-pinned in the new describe with the unread-request half kept (`bodyUsed === false`, exact bytes) and the body half moved to the new answer (`readRefusal` reads the handed-on value through `JSON.stringify` and asserts `status 400`, `INVALID_REQUEST` and the media-type message; the form row asserts `{ token: 'def', x: '1' }`); a no-`Content-Type` row and the cache-path row are added. Every remaining reference row, the `no Content-Type at all` string row included (undici types it `text/plain;charset=UTF-8`, no framing header, so both the reference line and the new reader answer `{}`), is unchanged.
- The explicit `Content-Length` on in-process rows is what the twin's own suite does (`request-body-refusal.test.ts:100`); the row "an in-process text/plain body with no framing headers" pins that both doors read it as no body, so the framing is declared, not hidden.
- Red at base, green at head, and two ablations that partition the 25 red cases 17 plus 8 by row group, each restore proven by blob: reported; consistent with the diff.

**8. Legitimate callers.** None refused in what can be read from here. `packages/client` defaults `Content-Type: application/json`; the console at the pinned objectui sha `f8267df93aba` declares JSON on every body-carrying call the dev enumerated, which is the set the #24005 records (`6221858698` item 7, `6222965551` item 4) verified at the same pin; `data-objectstack`'s multipart `uploadFile` / `uploadFiles` have no caller at the pin and no server route. The cloud host is NOT MEASURED (③ item 7).
